inspection_method: Direct inspection of diagnostic curves, six uniformly spaced overview frames, three consecutive six-frame full-image sheets and their native-resolution ROI sheets. Saved visualization timestamps were programmatically decoded and checked.
scope_limit: Contact-sheet and ROI inspection, not complete real-time video playback or examination of every native-resolution pixel.
selection: Six uniform overview frames; two non-overlapping high-T windows plus fixed middle window. ROI is fixed image coordinates, not object tracking. Post-hoc diagnostic selection.

findings.finding: Large tracks, supports and the train remain separable from the sky; fine passenger/seat/rail gaps often merge.

At frames 14, 15 and 16, train and neighboring rail values alternate lighter/darker/lighter while RGB motion remains continuous. Fixed display limits rule out per-frame color rescaling. No GT is available to measure how much change is erroneous.
Frames 32-37 retain coarse pole outlines with more subtle local changes; evidence does not support claiming that every edge flickers.
Late train descent and trees entering the image also change whole-frame quantiles; real motion and scene composition must be distinguished from prediction instability.

All frame medians are zero because exact-zero relative output covers 66.76-75.44 percent of each frame. This statistic cannot establish temporal stability. Finite zeros are valid relative values, not zero meters.

prior_user_observations: Preserved as preliminary context. These findings were independently checked against current arrays and visual evidence rather than accepted from prior user wording.
limitations: No video depth GT. T is not depth accuracy; whole-frame quantile changes also reflect scene composition. Zero relative values are finite model output, not invalid metric depths.
